question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $71u+22v=\text{gcd}(71,22).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}71 & = & 22\cdot 3 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 22 & = & 5\cdot 4 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(22,71)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =71-22\cdot 3 \\ 2 & =22-5\cdot 4 \\ 1 & =5-2\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-2\cdot 2 \\  & =5-[22-5\cdot 4]\cdot 2 \\  & =5\cdot 9-22\cdot 2 \\  & =[71-22\cdot 3]\cdot 9-22\cdot 2 \\  & =71\cdot 9-22\cdot 29 \\  & =71\cdot 9+22\cdot (-29)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-29.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=9+(-29)=-20.
$$
